claims.text: Helm is a graduated Cloud Native Computing Foundation project.
Helm is open source under Apache License 2.0 and the Helm project does not ship a commercial tier.
Helm installs resources in a fixed order by Kubernetes kind, defined in helm/helm pkg/release/v1/util/kind_sorter.go.
Helm chart authors can't declare dependencies between resources or subcharts, except through hook weights.
In Pulumi, each resource waits for its dependencies to become ready, and independent resources deploy in parallel.

The Helm docs state that "the Kubernetes objects from the charts and all its dependencies are aggregated into a single set; then sorted by type followed by name; and then created/updated in that order."

Helm's install order is a hardcoded list of Kubernetes kinds beginning with PriorityClasses and Namespaces, then Secrets and ConfigMaps, then CustomResourceDefinitions and RBAC, then Services and workloads, with unlisted kinds (including custom resources) last.
Helm uninstall runs the kind-sorted list in reverse order.
Helm sends the sorted manifests to the API server in a single pass and doesn't wait for one resource to become ready before applying the next.
Helm chart dependencies don't change ordering: a subchart's objects are merged into the parent chart's set and sorted by kind.
Helm hook resources are not managed by Helm as part of the release, and hooks are ordered with helm.sh/hook-weight annotations.
Native sequencing for resources and subcharts has been proposed in HIP-0025, which is still a draft.
Passing one resource's output into another or setting the dependsOn resource option creates an edge in Pulumi's dependency graph.
The Pulumi Kubernetes provider waits for each resource to become ready before creating dependents and deploys independent resources in parallel; deletes follow the graph in reverse.
Pulumi's helm.v4.Chart supports the config.kubernetes.io/depends-on annotation for ordering between objects inside the chart, and dependsOn on the chart for dependencies on outside resources.

Helm merges objects from a chart and its dependencies into a single set, sorts them by Kubernetes kind, and applies them in that order, so declaring a subchart dependency doesn't make it install first.
A failed Pulumi update leaves the stack partially updated, and you roll forward by reverting program code and running pulumi up.
Helm SDK is available in Go only; other languages must shell out to the helm CLI.
Two patterns cover most production deployments of Pulumi and Helm together.
Using Helm charts directly from a Pulumi program is the most common adoption pattern.

helm.v4.Chart renders templates locally and registers each Kubernetes object as an individual Pulumi resource, so children show in plan output, drift detection, and state; helm.v3.Release uses the embedded Helm SDK and creates a real Helm release preserving hooks, post-rendering, and release history.
Pulumi resolves chart values at deploy time and orders the chart install after the resources it depends on.
Pulumi Policies is open source, with rules in Python, TypeScript, or OPA Rego; Enterprise edition adds Pulumi-maintained policy packs for CIS, PCI DSS, HITRUST, and NIST.
